one_line: Amazon's API for sellers/vendors to manage listings, orders, inventory, fulfillment, pricing, reports and merchant services at scale.
auth_notes: OAuth2 via Login with Amazon (LWA) to get a refresh token per selling partner, then AWS SigV4-signed requests with IAM role/credentials; requires a registered SP-API application with role(s) assigned per seller.
self_serve_notes: A dev with a professional seller account (~$39.99/mo) or vendor account can self-register in Seller Central > Partner Network > SP-API and create apps; each role (e.g., Listings, Orders, Fulfillment) requires separate registration and approval.

api_surface.breadth_estimate: 40+ distinct SP-API sections (Orders, Feeds, Reports, Product Pricing, Inventory, Fulfillment, Merchant Fulfillment, Listings Items/Restrictions, Catalog Items, Finances, Merchant Fulfillment, Notifications, etc.) with hundreds of endpoints; OpenAPI specs published on GitHub
api_surface.webhook_note: SP-API Notifications (order/listing/report lifecycle events) pushed via destination SQS/SNS/EventBridge instead of classic webhooks

existing_mcp.note: No official Amazon MCP server; community SP-API MCP servers exist on GitHub/MCP registries

evidence.note: Fetched text confirms SP-API docs portal for sellers/vendors with API references, models, notifications and GitHub swagger models; LWA OAuth + SigV4 from knowledge

agent_notes: Auth is the most complex (LWA + SigV4 + IAM + per-role registration). Self-serve but registration/approval per role adds days; needs a paid professional seller account.
